rationale: The dormant-renderer strategy correctly separates the deliverable surface (app-side: knownTools + CodexSubagentView + toolViewRegistry) from the protocol-side blocker (sessionProtocolMapper branches require Codex CLI changes that are out of scope).

When Codex eventually emits subagent events, only sessionProtocolMapper.ts needs branch additions following the documented exec_command_begin template — no rework of the app-side renderers needed. This is the correct architectural seam.

5 knownTools + 1 view + 5 _all.tsx entries + 1 TODO comment is the correct minimal surface. Each piece is necessary: knownTools makes the inline card render, _all.tsx routes detail-panel to CodexSubagentView, the view itself branches on tool.name (spawn_agent → TaskStatusRow vs control-plane → degenerate sidebar). Removing any one piece would create a broken-when-activated state.

The strategy also matches the Phase B BA's independent finding (BA spec line 20: 'Phase B BA (concurrent pipeline) independently confirmed the same limitation: 7 of 9 Phase B tools are protocol-blocked.') — strong cross-pipeline corroboration of the protocol-blocked state.
